title: Shopify vs BigCommerce
description: A workflow-fit comparison of Shopify and BigCommerce as e-commerce platforms. Compare catalog and product management, checkout, storefront customization, order operations, payment options, shipping workflows, integrations, migration effort, and total cost for the plans you would actually use. The best fit depends on your store model and operating requirements, not an unsupported universal score.

features.name: Free tier availability
features.tool1Detail: Shopify offers a free tier with essential features for getting started. Free tiers include core functionality with usage limits.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides a trial period for evaluation. Freemium models reduce initial investment risk.

features.name: Entry-level pricing
features.tool1Detail: Shopify starts at Free Trial ($29–$299/mo + fees). This tier supports small teams with core features. See Finance & Accounting pricing guide.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce begins at Paid ($39 – $399/mo). TCO should include per-user fees, storage overages, and premium add-ons.

features.name: Enterprise pricing
features.tool1Detail: Shopify offers custom enterprise pricing with SLA-backed support and advanced security. Includes audit logging and data residency.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides enterprise tiers with volume discounts. SSO, compliance certs, and custom SLAs included.

features.name: Annual discount
features.tool1Detail: Shopify offers 15-20% savings with annual billing. TCO cost reduction for committed teams with multi-year contract options.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides annual billing with 15-25% savings. SaaS pricing analysis confirms typical annual commitment benefits.

features.name: Free trial duration
features.tool1Detail: Shopify provides a 14-30 day free trial with access to all core features. This trial period allows teams to thoroughly evaluate the platform against their specific workflows, test integrations with existing tools, and assess overall performance before making a financial commitment. Many teams use this period to run parallel operations and validate migration paths.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce offers a similar trial duration with full feature access. We strongly recommend our structured evaluation checklist to maximize trial effectiveness, including checking integration compatibility, testing API endpoints, and evaluating performance under your typical workload conditions.

features.name: Contract flexibility
features.tool1Detail: Shopify offers month-to-month, annual, and multi-year contract options. Monthly billing provides flexibility for teams still evaluating fit, while annual contracts reduce per-unit costs. SaaS contract terms typically include usage-based scaling and add-on modules.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides flexible contract terms with monthly and annual options. Multi-year commitments often include additional discounts and waived implementation fees for enterprise customers.

features.name: Usage-based scaling
features.tool1Detail: Shopify scales pricing based on team size, storage, and feature tier. Usage-based pricing ensures you only pay for what you need, with automatic upgrades as your team grows. Industry benchmarks help forecast costs at scale.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce offers similar usage-based scaling with clear upgrade paths. TCO modeling should include expected growth over 12-24 months when comparing platforms.

features.name: User role management
features.tool1Detail: Shopify provides RBAC with customizable permission levels supporting complex hierarchies and compliance.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce offers role management with SCIM provisioning for SSO-based user lifecycle management.

features.name: Two-factor authentication
features.tool1Detail: Shopify supports 2FA via TOTP, SMS, and FIDO2 hardware keys. Zero-trust benefits from MFA enforcement.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides 2FA with authenticator apps and biometrics on mobile. Encryption combined with 2FA provides defense-in-depth.

features.name: Audit logging
features.tool1Detail: Shopify maintains audit trails for actions and changes. Compliance-ready exports support SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides activity logging with searchable history. SIEM integration enables centralized monitoring.

features.name: Mobile app
features.tool1Detail: Shopify offers native iOS and Android apps with push notifications and offline access for mobile workforce productivity.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides mobile apps. Remote team collaboration supported via mobile-optimized interfaces.

features.name: Search functionality
features.tool1Detail: Shopify features full-text search with filters. AI-powered search suggests relevant results based on usage patterns.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides search with filtering. Global search helps teams find information across workspaces.

features.name: Template library
features.tool1Detail: Shopify provides pre-built templates for common workflows. Custom templates support branding and standardization.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce offers template collections for industries. Workflow templates speed implementation.

features.name: Community ecosystem
features.tool1Detail: Shopify has a large community. Community contributions extend functionality via plugins and shared resources.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce maintains growing community with user groups and forums.

features.name: Onboarding experience
features.tool1Detail: Shopify offers guided onboarding with tutorials and setup wizards. Self-paced learning accelerates proficiency.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides documentation, video tutorials, and live training. Knowledge base covers setup scenarios.

features.name: Multi-language support
features.tool1Detail: Shopify supports multiple languages with localized interfaces. International teams benefit from regional format support.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides multi-language with interface translations. i18n supports global collaboration.

features.name: Custom branding
features.tool1Detail: Shopify provides white-label options with custom domain and branding for client portals.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce offers branding customization with custom themes and domain config on business plans.

features.name: Bulk operations
features.tool1Detail: Shopify supports batch processing for data management. API-based bulk operations handle large datasets efficiently, with progress tracking and error reporting built into the workflow.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce offers bulk import/export in CSV and JSON formats. Scheduled bulk operations support automated data synchronization between systems.

features.name: Data portability
features.tool1Detail: Shopify provides full data export capabilities in multiple formats including JSON, CSV, and PDF. API-based data access ensures you maintain control of your information at all times. GDPR data portability requirements are fully supported.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce supports data portability through export tools and API access. Migration in or out of the platform is designed to minimize friction for growing teams.

features.name: Offline mode
features.tool1Detail: Shopify provides offline functionality with automatic sync when connectivity is restored. This is critical for field teams, traveling professionals, and environments with unreliable internet access.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce offers limited offline capabilities with local caching of recent data. Mobile apps provide the most robust offline experience for on-the-go teams.

features.name: SSO/SAML
features.tool1Detail: Shopify supports SSO via SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning for AD sync.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce offers SSO on mid-tier plans with social login options.

features.name: Encryption at rest
features.tool1Detail: Shopify uses AES-256 encryption with CMEK on enterprise plans. Data residency controls included.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce encrypts with AES-256 with auto key rotation. SOC 2 standards are met.

features.name: Encryption in transit
features.tool1Detail: Shopify enforces TLS 1.3 with perfect forward secrecy.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce uses TLS with HTTPS-only API enforcement.

features.name: SOC 2 Type II
features.tool1Detail: Shopify maintains SOC 2 Type II with annual independent audits.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce is SOC 2 certified with regular assessments.

features.name: GDPR compliance
features.tool1Detail: Shopify is GDPR compliant with DPA and EU data residency options.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides GDPR features with DPA and data portability.

features.name: HIPAA compliance
features.tool1Detail: Shopify has not independently verified HIPAA compliance — contact vendor for current status.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce has not independently verified HIPAA compliance — contact vendor for current status.

features.name: Uptime SLA
features.tool1Detail: Shopify guarantees 99.9% uptime with SLA credits. Multi-region redundancy ensures business continuity.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce offers competitive SLA commitments with SOC 2 audited availability metrics.

features.name: Data residency
features.tool1Detail: Shopify data residency options — not independently verified; contact vendor
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce data residency options — not independently verified; contact vendor

features.name: Incident response
features.tool1Detail: Shopify maintains a documented incident response plan with notification timelines aligned to SOC 2 requirements. Security incidents are communicated within SLA-defined windows.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce follows industry-standard incident response procedures with regular tabletop exercises and third-party penetration testing.

features.name: Vulnerability management
features.tool1Detail: Shopify runs continuous vulnerability scanning and maintains a responsible disclosure program. Third-party security audits are conducted quarterly with results available to enterprise customers.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce performs regular security assessments with automated scanning and manual penetration testing by certified security researchers.

features.name: API access
features.tool1Detail: Shopify provides REST and GraphQL APIs with SDKs. Webhooks enable event-driven integrations.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce offers RESTful API. Automation platforms connect both for no-code workflows.

features.name: Native integrations
features.tool1Detail: Shopify integrates with Slack, Jira, GitHub, Salesforce.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce offers API-first architecture for custom connector development.

features.name: Webhook support
features.tool1Detail: Shopify supports custom webhooks for event-driven workflows and real-time data sync.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides webhook triggers and actions for automation.

features.name: Auto workflow
features.tool1Detail: Shopify includes workflow automation for common tasks. Automation comparisons help choose complementary tools.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides automation with triggers and conditional logic for complex business processes.

features.name: Reporting and analytics
features.tool1Detail: Shopify offers custom dashboards and KPI tracking. Industry benchmarks contextualize metrics.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides reporting with visual analytics and export. ROI tracking demonstrates value.

features.name: Notification system
features.tool1Detail: Shopify provides customizable alerts and push, email, and in-app notifications.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce offers notification controls with configurable triggers.

features.name: Customer support
features.tool1Detail: Shopify provides knowledge base, email, and chat. Premium tiers include SLA-backed support and account managers.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce offers ticket support and help center. Zendesk integration enables unified ticketing.

features.name: Training resources
features.tool1Detail: Shopify offers webinars, documentation, and certification programs for team upskilling.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce provides help center and video tutorials for self-paced learning.

features.name: Community support
features.tool1Detail: Shopify has large active community forums and user groups for peer support.
features.tool2Detail: BigCommerce maintains growing community with meetups and events.

verdict: This page is a decision guide rather than a verified scored ranking. To choose between Shopify and BigCommerce, test the same representative product catalog, checkout path, shipping and tax rules, discounts, integrations, and order-management tasks in both platforms. Compare the total cost at your expected sales volume, the flexibility needed for your storefront, how your existing systems connect, and how easily you can export data if you switch. Do not treat an unverified stored pick or feature row as proof of superiority.

faqs.question: Are Shopify and BigCommerce direct substitutes?
faqs.answer: Yes, they are both e-commerce platforms, but their plan limits, storefront workflows, ecosystem choices, and operating costs can differ. Test the same store requirements in both before deciding.

faqs.question: What should I test before choosing?
faqs.answer: Use a representative catalog and test product variants, checkout, discounts, taxes, shipping, returns, inventory updates, and the integrations your team needs. Record any required add-ons or manual work.

faqs.question: How should I compare pricing?
faqs.answer: Compare the exact plan for your store, payment processing and transaction fees, apps, themes, shipping tools, staff accounts, and expected sales volume. Recalculate costs as the store grows.

faqs.question: Can I migrate between Shopify and BigCommerce?
faqs.answer: Migration may require moving products, customers, orders, redirects, content, and integration settings. Confirm export formats and migration limitations with both vendors, and test redirects and checkout before changing the live store.

faqs.question: Which platform is the verified winner?
faqs.answer: This page does not claim an independently verified winner or score. Run the same store workflow in both products and select the platform that meets your must-have requirements with the least operational friction.

faqs.question: What is the most important decision factor?
faqs.answer: Start with your store model, catalog complexity, checkout and payment needs, fulfillment workflows, required integrations, and total cost at realistic volume. The right choice depends on which of these requirements is non-negotiable.
